newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran seeks Gulf Arab help on marine environment.
newsitem.headline: Iran seeks Gulf Arab help on marine environment.

text.p: Iran, which has been moving to improve relations with its Gulf Arab neighbours, plans a task force to protect the region's marine environment, its environmental chief said.
Hadi Manafi, head of the Environmental Protection Agency, blamed large fleets of U.S. warships and frequent manoeuvres as major factors detrimental to the environment.

In remarks published in Tehran newspapers on Monday, he said the force would cooperate with neighbouring Iraq and member states of the Gulf Cooperation Council -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates.
All eight countries form the Regional Organisation for Protection of Marine Environment.
Manafi said the Gulf's relatively shallow waters and large number of coral islands were among reasons which made the strategic waterway suitable for fish farming.

Several marine species including sea turtles, dolphins and sharks were among protected species recognised by the Convention on International Trade on Endangered Species and the international convention on bio-diversity, he said.
Manafi said pollution levels in the Gulf were high and the navigation of oil tankers in regional waters and the presence of many foreign military ships threatened the fragile environment.
The United States keeps the largest foreign force in the Gulf to help enforce sanctions against Iraq and defend the Gulf Arab oil states.
Tehran Times daily said regional cooperation could be achieved only by establishing a maritime guard in regional countries' territorial and international waters.
But it said the United States seriously opposed any kind of regional cooperation and would likely undermine any move to forge a regional alliance for cooperation.
The United States and regional countries were aware that cooperation in non-political issues was easier than in politico-strategic issues and was a prelude to the latter.
